title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1971-04-28
lineage: SBD > MR > (Reel post-Bird Song) > Alesis Masterlink > CD-R

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a high‑energy Fillmore East night, highlighted by a blistering Hard to Handle and an unforgettable Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its pristine mix and almost perfect balance, with only occasional popping on the New Riders set. Musically the show is described as one of the best of the spring ’71 run – a scorching Hard to Handle, epic (though short) Dark Star, soaring Bird Song and Morning Dew, plus a powerful Bill Kreutzmann‑driven rhythm section. Despite a missing second half of The Other One and the absent Wharf Rat, reviewers consider this performance a quintessential Dead concert.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly enthusiastic 5‑star comments (plus a few 4‑star) emphasize both superb soundboard quality and an exceptional, high‑energy performance; minor issues are noted but do not detract from the overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, balanced mix praised by many reviewers; a few notes of slight popping on the New Riders set and missing tape‑flip portions of The Other One/Wharf Rat.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong, tight first set that builds momentum into a fiery second set; Dark Star segues into St. Stephen and the classic NFA > GDTRFB > NFA jam, delivering a powerful climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is highlighted as perfect; his solos are described as soaring and he corrects Bob’s lyric slip‑ups.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir adds percussion on Morning Dew, slips a lyric in St. Stephen (creating humorous moments), and shares vocal duties.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten sits in, providing crisp keyboard work on Dark Star and other jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann shines with frenetic, jaw‑dropping polyrhythms that drive the band’s intensity.
